title.narrative: Inner Mongolia Sustainable Cross-Border Development Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative: The investment program will promote sustainable development of cross-border areas and mutually beneficial regional cooperation and integration between the PRC's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region (IMAR) and Mongolia. The program will improve economic inclusion, ecosystems, and basic social services in the five IMAR border crossing point (BCP) communities and surrounding areas on both sides of the 3,200-kilometer (km) PRC-Mongolia frontier, which lags in economic and social development. Expanded financial and business support to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in border regions will spur local income growth. Establishment of an agricultural value chain will enhance livelihoods on both sides of the frontier. The program will have strong regional spillover benefits to Mongolia: improvement in infrastructure and services at IMAR-Mongolia BCPs will boost the volume and quality of trade, creating about 3,300 direct and indirect jobs in Mongolia; and improvement in health and other services will benefit disadvantaged communities on both sides of the border.

Output: Cross-border mechanisms, technical project management and institutional capacity strengthened Indicator: Improved skills and knowledge on regional cooperation and services, project management, safeguards, and gender issues provided to at least 250 government officials, of whom at least 40% are women Progress/Status: Training activities have been conducted under Tranche 1 since 2021, with the assistance of individual consultants engaged by EA and ADB and the project management consulting firm. As of 30 June 2025, training on regional cooperation, project management, procurement, safeguards, financial management, and gender issues has been provided to more than 380 government officials and staff of EA, IAs, and implementing enterprises, of which 40% are women. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports and Tranche 1 project completion report by the executing agency and implementing agencies

Output: Ecological environment in key border towns improved Indicator: Coverage area of protective forest in Erenhot-Zamyn-Uud ECZ increased by 35.5 hectares Progress/Status: ECW5-1 Erenhot -Ecological protection greenbelt along the central axis, including reclaimed water storage and irrigation facilities, and landscape lighting, covers an area of 24.49 ha: construction is ongoing with 80% progress and will be completed in 2026. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports and Tranche 1 project completion report by the executing agency and implementing agencies Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y

Output: Sustainable infrastructure and services for cross-border connectivity improved Indicator: New smart port with one-stop inspection system established and operated at Erenhot Port Progress/Status: ECW1-2 for north plaza infrastructure: contract was awarded in Aug 2023; construction started in Sept 2023 with 80% completed as of July 2025; remaining works have been completed by the end of 2025.
ECW1-3 for south plaza infrastructure: contract was awarded in Sept 2023; construction started in Oct 2023 with 80% works completed; the remaining works have been completed by the end of 2025.
ECW1-4 for internal decoration and facilities of the inspection building: the contract was signed in January; construction was completed by the end of 2025.
ECW3-1 PRC-Mongolia Regional Cooperation Center, with a floor area of 20,000 m2 (with an updated cost estimate of $20.2 million): BD was received and approved in October 2025.
EG2-1-1 for basic infrastructure and equipment of the smart port management system: contract was awarded in May 2023, and all goods have been supplied, and installation completed to about 90%. The remaining installation works for ECW1-4 were in line with the contract and completed in 2026.
EG2-1-2 for the smart port management system: contract was signed, and PCSS was issued in August 2025.
EG4-1 for 66 sets of medical equipment was awarded in July-December 2022, and the equipment has been supplied to the hospital; 20 sets of medical equipment purchased using domestic funds due to urgent needs have been put into operation since 2020.
Data Source: Semiannual progress reports and Tranche 1 project completion report by the executing agency and implementing agencies Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y
